whyBuy.title: Why **Facebook Likes Drive Organic Reach for Every Post**
whyBuy.body:
Facebook's news feed algorithm decides which posts to show, to whom, and how prominently based on a combination of engagement signals collected in the hours after publishing. Likes are the most immediate and accessible of those signals. They are easy for users to give, easy for the algorithm to count, and directly tied to how widely Facebook distributes your content beyond your existing followers.

A post that collects likes quickly after publishing signals to Facebook that the content is resonating with its audience. Facebook responds by showing that post to more of your followers, and in some cases, to friends of people who engaged with it. A post that sits with no likes gets progressively buried in the feed, seen by fewer and fewer people over time regardless of how relevant or useful the content actually is.

For business pages specifically, this dynamic makes early post engagement a strategic priority. Every post you publish is competing with hundreds of other pieces of content for limited news feed space. Posts that signal early engagement quality win that competition. Posts that do not, lose visibility immediately and permanently.

Here is what stronger Facebook like counts do for your posts and page:

- Signal content quality to Facebook's algorithm, triggering wider news feed distribution
- Increase the chance your post is shown to friends of people who liked it through social graph distribution
- Create social proof that encourages real users to stop scrolling and engage with your content
- Improve your page's overall engagement rate, which Facebook uses as a long-term authority signal
- Make your posts look credible and active to new visitors checking your page for the first time
- Reduce the need for paid boosting by maximising the organic reach of every post you publish

faq.title: Frequently Asked **Questions About Buying Facebook Likes**

items.question: Do Facebook likes help posts reach more people?
items.answer: Yes. Facebook's algorithm uses likes as one of its primary early engagement signals when deciding how widely to distribute a post through the news feed. A post that collects likes quickly after publishing signals content quality to the algorithm, triggering wider distribution to more of your followers and in some cases to friends of people who engaged. Posts without early likes get progressively buried regardless of content quality.

items.question: Will buying Facebook likes get my page banned?
items.answer: No page has ever been banned solely for receiving likes through SMMGen. Facebook's policies target coordinated inauthentic behaviour and spam through clearly deceptive methods. SMMGen delivers likes using profile types and pacing that align with natural post engagement patterns. Every order also includes a 30-day refill guarantee to cover any drops from Facebook's routine engagement quality audits.

items.question: Do likes matter more than comments on Facebook?
items.answer: Both likes and comments contribute to Facebook's engagement signal but in different ways. Likes are the most immediate signal and the easiest for users to give. Comments carry more individual weight because they require active effort. The strongest Facebook posts combine both. For a complete engagement strategy, combining like orders with strong content that encourages real comments gives the best organic reach results. If you also want to grow your page audience, visit our buy Facebook followers page.

items.answer: Yes. SMMGen supports like delivery for any public Facebook post regardless of format or when it was published. Text posts, image posts, video posts, shared links, and event posts are all supported. Your post must be publicly visible before placing your order. Both new posts and older posts can receive likes through SMMGen.

items.question: How many likes is good on a Facebook post?
items.answer: Benchmarks vary significantly by page size and industry. As a general guide, a page with 1,000 followers performing well might expect 20 to 50 likes per post. A page with 10,000 followers would consider 200 to 500 likes strong performance. The most important metric is your like rate as a percentage of your total followers. A like rate above 2% is considered healthy engagement for Facebook pages in most niches.

Facebook page likes are a measure of overall page credibility and appear publicly on your page as a trust signal to new visitors. Both serve different purposes.
